newsitem.title: UK: Ofwat says MidKent bid block best for UK customers.
newsitem.headline: Ofwat says MidKent bid block best for UK customers.

text.p: Britain's water industry regulator, Ofwat, said on Tuesday it was in full agreement with the earlier decision by the Department of Trade and Industry to block a planned takeover by two French utility groups of a small English water company, Mid Kent Holdings Plc.

Ian Byatt, Ofwat's director general, said in a statement he believed the decision was in the best interests of customers and would allow a better solution of what he called "the water resource problem" in south-eastern England.

"Saur (part of construction group Bouygues) and General Utilities (Generals des Eaux) proposed the takeover of Mid Kent as a way of addressing the resource shortages faced by their companies operating in the south east.
"I was not convinced, however, that the merger was necessary to bring about a satisfactory solution to these problems," Byatt said in his statement.

He went on to stress that, after the blocking, it was important that Ofwat and other agencies sorted out the issue and added that no solution was likely to be effective without the active involvement of the large Southern Water Plc.
"I have powers to require companies to make supplies available in bulk to other companies who need them," he said, adding other alternatives included changing firms' licenses.
In another statement, Mid Kent said it also welcomed the decision which brought to a close over 12 months of uncertainty for the company.

"We remain commited to delivering performance gains to both our shareholders and to our customers," the company said, adding its board had "every confidence in the future trading prospects of Mid Kent as an independent company".
